goal: Let the user confirm a destructive action before it happens
how: A .modal--sm the page writes, its heading the question, its body naming what will be lost, and its footer Cancel then the action repeated on a filled danger button. ShowModalAsync returns the value of the button pressed, and Escape comes back as null.
avoid: Yes and No on the buttons: the confirming button repeats the action, so the reader knows what they agreed to without reading the question again.

goal: Let the user answer a dialog's question before anything else happens
how: A dialog.modal opened with showModal(), aria-labelledby on its heading, header, body and footer rows, and the whole panel in a form method="dialog" so each button closes it with its value. The platform gives the top layer, the focus trap, Escape and focus back on close.
avoid: A div with a backdrop of the app's own for something that can be a dialog: the focus trap, Escape and the inert page behind are then the app's to write.

goal: Let the user edit a record in a dialog and come back to the page with the result
how: A component of its own that writes a dialog.modal with its form, presented with ISednaOverlays.ShowAsync from one SednaOverlayHost in the layout and closed with Overlay.CloseAsync(result). data-close-guard asks before Escape throws away what was typed.
avoid: Rendering the dialog component inline in the page and opening it through a @ref: it is rendered on every visit and its state outlives each opening.

goal: Let the user get started through a short welcome before using the app
how: A .modal.deck of a few slides, one rendered at a time and keyed on the step, with a dot button per step marked aria-current="step", the position in words, and Back and Next. A tour of the page itself follows once the reader has seen it.
avoid: A deck of more than a few slides: what the reader needs to start is short, and the rest is better shown on the page itself.

goal: Let the user open a record in a side panel without losing their place in the list
how: A dialog.drawer opened with showModal(), its header the record's lockup with .list-row--flush, everything that scrolls in .drawer-body and its decision in .drawer-footer. The list stays behind it, so closing it puts the reader back on the row.
avoid: Using a drawer for a question that must be answered first: dismissing a drawer loses nothing, and a question that cannot be dismissed is a modal.

goal: Let the user pull a sheet up from the bottom of a phone screen
how: A dialog.drawer.sheet with data-sheet, a .sheet-handle the reader drags and data-sheet-snap for the heights it rests at. Written as a button with data-sheet-expand, the handle is the keyboard's way to the next height, and a close button is still what dismisses it.
avoid: Leaving the close button out because the sheet can be swiped down: a swipe is no way out for a keyboard or a switch.

goal: Let the user choose one of a record's actions from a sheet on a phone
phrases: actions from the bottom of the screen
how: A .sheet whose body is .drawer-body--flush holding a list of button.list-row, each an icon, the action and a second line saying what it will do; the header names the record.
avoid: A sheet for two or three short actions on a pointer screen, which a menu under the button does with less.

goal: Let the user find and run any command by typing its name
how: The app writes the palette's dialog once in its layout and registers what is available with sednaUi.palette.register, again whenever that changes; the library wires Ctrl+K, ranks the matches and runs the one chosen.
avoid: Registering commands the reader may not run: register() replaces the list, so call it after the permission check.

goal: Let the user learn a page through a guided tour of its controls
how: The app's own .spotlight-hole and .spotlight-tip with its steps, kept attached to each target by FollowSpotlightAsync; the bubble has a way out that is not Next, and the position in words as .spotlight-step.
avoid: Treating a locked step as a security boundary: lock() stops a person's pointer, never a script.

goal: Let the user notice one control the first time they see it
how: One hole over the control and one bubble saying what it is for, with a single button to dismiss it and no step counter; at() places them where the target is known only at runtime.
avoid: A step counter on a single hint: 1 of 1 promises a tour that is not coming.
